name: Authentication, student registration and session lifecycle
description: Verify provider-managed first-time account creation, returning login, profile setup, session persistence and logout.
steps: Open a clean signed-out browser session and visit ExpenseBuddy
Verify private finance records are not rendered before authentication
Use the hosted AppDeploy login page and create a new QA identity using email verification
Verify the identity provider prevents duplicate accounts for an existing email and returns the user to the existing identity
Complete first-time onboarding with a full name and verify the authenticated email is displayed as read-only
Refresh and verify the authenticated session and student profile are restored
Sign out and verify protected content is hidden
Sign in again with the same identity and verify the same profile and records are loaded
expected: The provider creates or reuses a unique verified identity, first-time onboarding creates one student profile, refresh restores the session, and logout clears access. Authentication is passwordless email/provider-managed; the application must not collect passwords.

name: Expense and category lifecycle, validation, search and filters
description: Exercise transaction and category workflows end-to-end, including negative inputs and category integrity.
steps: Verify Food, Transportation, Education, Shopping, Entertainment, Healthcare, Accommodation, Utilities and Other default expense categories
Create a QA custom category and verify it appears in the category selector
Create an expense with title, amount, category, date and description; verify it appears in history and details
Edit the expense and verify updated fields persist after reload
Create an income transaction and verify its transaction type and amount
Search by title and description; verify matching results
Apply category, transaction type, date range, minimum and maximum amount filters; verify results
Attempt blank title, zero/negative amount, invalid date, and invalid category submissions; verify rejection
Attempt duplicate custom category creation and verify a clear conflict response
Attempt to delete or rename a category that is referenced by transactions and verify it is safely blocked
Delete the QA transaction and then delete the now-unused custom category
expected: Valid transactions and categories persist, search and filters narrow the expected results, invalid payloads are rejected, and category references are not broken.

name: Monthly budgets, calculations, threshold alerts and dashboard charts
description: Verify deterministic monthly finance calculations and alert thresholds using dedicated QA data.
steps: Choose a QA month without a budget and verify the no-budget state
Set a budget of 10000 and add expense records totaling 7500
Verify expenses=7500, remaining=2500 and utilization=75 percent; verify the 75 percent alert
Increase expenses to 9000 and verify the 90 percent alert
Increase expenses to 10000 and verify the 100 percent alert and exceeded state
Reload and verify already-delivered threshold alerts are not repeated
Edit the budget and verify previously delivered threshold markers remain recorded
Select another month and verify its budget and expense calculations are independent
Record income and verify dashboard income totals update
Verify monthly spending, category breakdown and income-versus-expense charts reflect the actual QA records
Verify no sample or fabricated amounts are presented as the student's actual data
expected: All monthly totals and percentages match the QA transactions, alert thresholds are delivered once, budget records remain month-specific and charts show stored user data.

name: Reports, savings goals, profile and settings
description: Verify reporting, savings and student profile workflows with safe handling of untrusted transaction text.
steps: Create a QA savings goal and add a contribution; verify saved amount and progress
Reload and verify the savings goal persists
Update profile name, institution and preferred currency; reload and verify persistence
Verify account email comes from the authenticated identity and is read-only
Create QA transactions in the selected month and a different month
Export CSV and verify only the selected month's matching report records are included
Verify cells beginning with spreadsheet formula characters are neutralized
Open PDF/print export and verify selected-month totals and transaction rows
Use a description containing HTML-like text and verify it is displayed as inert text in the report
Verify Settings clearly explains passwordless provider authentication and does not advertise a nonfunctional password-change form
Remove QA data after verifying exports
expected: Savings and profile changes persist, CSV and PDF exports reflect the selected month, and untrusted values are safe in exported documents.

name: Backend authorization, data isolation and validation
description: Exercise backend authorization with two independent QA identities and direct authenticated API requests.
steps: Actor A signs in and creates a uniquely named transaction, custom category, budget and savings goal
Record the returned record IDs
Actor A signs out and Actor B signs in using a different identity
Attempt to read, update and delete Actor A record IDs as Actor B
Attempt to spoof Actor A profile identity or email as Actor B
Verify Actor B cannot read or modify Actor A records and sees only Actor B data
Submit missing title, invalid amount, impossible date, invalid month, unsupported currency and unknown category payloads
Verify backend rejects invalid values and does not create partial records
Verify category deletion/rename and monthly budget uniqueness checks fail closed if the relevant table read is incomplete
Sign back in as Actor A and verify original records are unchanged
expected: Protected APIs enforce ownership using the verified identity; cross-account access fails; invalid data and incomplete safety checks are rejected without corrupting existing records.

name: Responsive, reliability and compatibility regression
description: Regression checks across viewports and key reliability paths.
steps: Open at 320px, 375px and 390px widths and verify there is no page-level horizontal overflow
Open at 768px tablet width and desktop width and verify navigation, charts, cards and tables adapt
Navigate every sidebar destination and verify no broken or inert navigation items
Verify tables scroll within their own container rather than forcing page overflow
Use keyboard navigation and verify focus indicators; enable reduced motion and verify animations are reduced
Simulate a failed API save and verify a useful error appears without a false success toast
Double-submit an expense form and verify only one transaction is created
Test month/date defaults at midnight and on the first day of a month in Asia/Karachi; verify local date/month is selected
Run the viewport checks in current Chrome, Firefox and Edge
expected: The app remains usable without page-level overflow, failures are surfaced safely, duplicate writes are guarded, and date defaults follow the student's local timezone. Browser checks must be individually recorded rather than inferred from a deployment smoke check.

name: Historical data limits, performance and operational recovery
description: Verify explicit operating boundaries and record evidence for performance and recovery rather than assuming these requirements are met.
steps: Use a QA account with enough records to cross a 500-item collection boundary
Verify the application warns that bootstrap data is incomplete and does not claim full-history totals
Verify budget alert calculations refuse to proceed when the complete expense history is unavailable
Measure authenticated cold and warm page loads under a documented normal test environment
Verify records survive logout, login and browser refresh
Review SECURITY-OPERATIONS.md for the configured backup and restore limitations
Do not mark backup/recovery complete until a platform backup and an actual restore have been demonstrated
expected: Incomplete record collections are clearly disclosed, performance results are measured, persistent data survives sessions, and backup/recovery remains explicitly unverified unless a restore drill succeeds.
